# [CS009] Unscoped Resource Mutation (IDOR) (idor-unscoped-mutation)

A record is updated or deleted by an ID from the request without an owner condition.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Severity** | MEDIUM |
| **Category** | Security |
| **CWE** | [CWE-639](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/639.html) |
| **OWASP** | A01:2025 |
| **Auto-Fix supported** | No |

## Why It Matters in Go

When a handler deletes or updates by an ID from the URL alone, any authenticated user can change other users' records by guessing IDs. Scope the statement to the caller: add the owner or tenant from the session to the WHERE clause and check the number of affected rows.

## Vulnerable / Problematic Example

```go
func deleteNote(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	_, _ = db.ExecContext(r.Context(), "DELETE FROM notes WHERE id = $1", r.PathValue("id"))
}
```

## Safe / Idiomatic Go Pattern

```go
func deleteNote(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	userID := session.UserID(r.Context())
	res, err := db.ExecContext(r.Context(), "DELETE FROM notes WHERE id = $1 AND owner_id = $2", r.PathValue("id"), userID)
	if n, _ := res.RowsAffected(); err != nil || n == 0 {
		http.NotFound(w, r)
	}
}
```

## Configuration & Suppression

Disable the rule for the whole module in `.codexsentinel.yaml`:

```yaml
rules:
  disabled: [idor-unscoped-mutation]
```

Change its severity:

```yaml
rules:
  severity_overrides:
    idor-unscoped-mutation: low
```

Suppress one reviewed finding on its line, with the reason:

```go
//codex:ignore idor-unscoped-mutation -- <reason>
```

Or ignore it under a path in `.codexsentinel.ignore`:

```text
internal/legacy/** idor-unscoped-mutation
```
